query: How are cancer trials distributed by country?

assumptions: 'Cancer trials' = studies whose registered condition matches 'cancer'.

Countries are the distinct site locations of each study; a multinational trial counts once in each country.
Only the 20 countries with the most trials are shown.

definitions.condition_match: Studies are matched with ClinicalTrials.gov's condition search, which includes its own synonym expansion (e.g. 'lung cancer' also matches 'NSCLC').
definitions.unit: Each bar/point/edge counts distinct studies (NCT IDs), never sites or arms.
definitions.country: Distinct site countries per study; a multinational study counts once in each of its countries.
definitions.multi_valued: A study listing several country values counts once in each, so counts can sum to more than the number of studies.

assumptions: 'Cancer trials' = studies whose registered condition matches 'cancer'.
The full cancer literature is too large to aggregate at once, so the view is restricted to currently recruiting interventional trials.
Countries are the distinct site locations of each study; a multinational trial counts once in each country.
Only the 20 countries with the most trials are shown.
'Recruiting' means overall status RECRUITING only; 'not yet recruiting' and 'enrolling by invitation' studies are not included.
warnings: Showing the top 20 of 110 country values by study count.
